title: Exactness data for the ringed-topos projection mate
statement:
Let $f:(\mathscr X,R_X)\to(\mathscr Y,R_Y)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi presented by small ringed sites, with sheaves of commutative rings and a ring map $f^{-1}R_Y\to R_X$. Use the abelian categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], K-flat resolutions [def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-pc-kflat-resolution], and direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Derived tensor is computed by replacing one factor by a K-flat resolution. Write $L=Lf^*$ for derived extension of scalars after inverse image and $R=Rf_*$ for the derived direct image computed using K-injective resolutions [def-pur-kinjective-complex, prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], with their canonical derived adjunction and counit $\varepsilon:LR\to1$. Derived tensor is exact in each variable. The canonical pullback tensor isomorphism
$$\mu_{M,N}:L(M\otimes^L_{R_Y}N)\xrightarrow{\sim}LM\otimes^L_{R_X}LN$$
is natural, unital, and compatible with the canonical integer-shift structures. For every $E\in D(R_X)$, the functors $F(P)=RE\otimes^L_{R_Y}P$ and $G(P)=R(E\otimes^L_{R_X}LP)$ are exact, and the natural transformation $\alpha:F\to G$ adjoint to $(\varepsilon_E\otimes1)\mu_{RE,P}$ commutes with these shift structures: if $s_F:F(P[1])\cong F(P)[1]$ and $s_G:G(P[1])\cong G(P)[1]$, then
$$s_G\alpha_{P[1]}=\alpha_P[1]s_F.$$
Consequently applying $\alpha$ to a distinguished triangle gives a morphism of distinguished triangles, including its connecting square. These structures are natural in $E$ and $P$; under the tensor-unit identifications $L(R_Y)=R_X$ and $RE\otimes^L R_Y=RE$, one has $\alpha_{R_Y}=1_{RE}$.

proof.text: The cited K-flat descent and resolutions construct derived tensor. The cited derived-pullback theorem constructs exact $L$; K-injective existence and the right-derived triangulated theorem construct exact $R$. The module adjunction and derived-adjoint theorem give $L\dashv R$. Its unit/counit and adjunct formula are those of the natural-bijection adjunction lemma.

proof.text: The fixed-K-flat lemma and resolutions give exact derived tensor with coherent shifts in both variables, hence exact $F,G$. Take $\mu$ from the derived pullback-tensor theorem. On resolving models its cochain comparison is the cited pullback-coherence map; it preserves the unsigned shift and the second-factor scalar $(-1)^{np}$. Its unit equation descends by tensor descent. The ring complex is K-flat since tensoring with it is the identity. Thus $L(R_Y)=R_X$ and $\mu$ is unital and shift-compatible.

proof.text: Put $H(P)=E\otimes^LLP$, $\beta=(\varepsilon_E\otimes1)\mu_{RE,-}$ and $\alpha=R\beta\circ\eta_F$, the adjunct formula. The derived-adjunction shift lemma makes $\eta$ shift-compatible. Step 2 and fixed-variable naturality of tensor shifts make $\beta$ shift-compatible. The composition/whiskering lemma makes $\eta_F$, $R\beta$ and their composite shift-compatible. Hence $s_G\alpha_{P[n]}=\alpha_P[n]s_F$ for every integer $n$, with the coherent composite comparisons.

proof.text: Naturality of $\beta$ and $\eta$ gives $G(u)\alpha_P=R(\beta_{P'}LF(u))\eta_{FP}=\alpha_{P'}F(u)$. For $e:E\to E'$, counit naturality gives $\beta^{E'}L(R(e)\otimes1)=(e\otimes1)\beta^E$; applying $R$ and unit naturality gives naturality of $\alpha$ in $E$.

proof.text: For a distinguished triangle with connecting map $w:P_3\to P_1[1]$, Step 2 makes both image triangles distinguished. Naturality gives their first two squares; the last is $\alpha_{P_1}[1]s_FF(w)=s_G\alpha_{P_1[1]}F(w)=s_GG(w)\alpha_{P_3}$. This is a morphism of triangles by the cited definition.

proof.text: Write $\rho$ for right unitors. Step 2 gives $\rho_{LM}(1\otimes\lambda)\mu_{M,R_Y}=L\rho_M$. Unitor naturality therefore identifies $\beta_{R_Y}$ with $\varepsilon_E$. Unit naturality and the adjunction triangle identity identify its adjunct with $R\varepsilon_E\circ\eta_{RE}=1_{RE}$, proving the required unit normalization.

The item statement is unchanged; its proof is now six steps totalling 2220 characters, as the human re-split note of 2026-10-21 asked (the old proof was 8001). I checked the source: Stacks 0B56 (sites-cohomology l.13666-13679) defines the projection map as the adjoint of the map built from Lf^*Rf_*E→E with 07A4/07A6. That is the item's α = adjunct of (ε_E⊗1)μ, with the same direction and the same coefficients (module sheaves over commutative rings, unbounded D). Steps: (1) the construction of ⊗^L, L, R and L⊣R is the base step compressed; (2) exact tensor comes from the new child, and μ on resolving models is the c_{u;P,Q} of pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence, which preserves bidegrees and so commutes with the unsigned first shift and the (-1)^{np} second-factor sign; the unitor equation comes from that node's action-unitor clause, and R_Y[0] is K-flat; (3) α=Rβ∘η_F is shift-compatible by derived-adjunction-shift, Step 2, fixed-argument naturality from the child and CommShift leaf parts (i)-(iii); (4)-(6) naturality, the triangle morphism and α_{R_Y}=1 are genuinely elementary. There is no cycle and proof_deps equals the union of the uses. The new leaf lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-integer-shifts is exact: I read Mathlib BifunctorShift.lean lines 95, 156/165 (sign (n₁y).negOnePow), 199 (mixed sign), 234/281, 269/315 and 326, and the instance name is confirmed by Loogle. The new child lem-weil-pbc-kflat-fixed-tensor-triangulated is true: I recomputed the cone comparison sign on A^p⊗B^{q+1} and its projection, which agrees with the leaf's second-factor shift for n=1 under the connecting-map convention -p. It proves the item's 'tensor exact' conjunct, but as an independent lemma on one ringed site that carries old Step 3's real argument and takes no other item clause as a hypothesis, so I do not count it as D1 relabelling.
